newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Four PNG ministers resign over mercenary crisis.
newsitem.headline: Four PNG ministers resign over mercenary crisis.

text.p: Four ministers in the cabinet of Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan resigned on Monday, piling more pressure on Chan himself to quit over his decision to hire foreign mercenaries.

The four, all opposed to the mercenary plan, tendered their resignation on Monday and said four more ministers in the 28-strong cabinet were expected to join them ahead of a proposed resolution against Chan in parliament on Tuesday.

Chan is facing a parliamentary motion, to be introduced by the opposition, to force him to resign over the $36 million contract with the British firm Sandline International for mercenaries to crush a rebellion on Bougainville island.

The ministers who tendered their resignation on Monday were Lands Minister Sir Albert Kipalan, Works and Transport Minister Peter Yama, Police Minister Castan Maibawa and Provincial Affairs Minister Peter Barter.

The ministers backed the army in its demand that Chan, deputy prime minister Chris Haiveta and Defence Minister Mathias Ijape should all resign before parliament resumes on Tuesday at two p.m. (0400 GMT).
"If the three of them don't go, then we will go," Kipalan told Reuters on Monday evening.
